title: Successive formations are separated by wide intervals of unrecorded time

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Successive formations are separated by wide intervals of unrecorded time

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The chief cause of the imperfection of the geological record is that successive geological formations are separated from each other by wide intervals of time during which no record was left.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But the imperfection in the geological record mainly results from another and more important cause than any of the foregoing; namely, from the several formations being separated from each other by wide intervals of time.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On the intermittence of geological formations”. Scope: sedimentary geological record worldwide

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Large public stratigraphic and fossil databases permit explicit quantification of hiatuses and sampling. The word 'mainly' requires modeling choices but is empirically assessable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify hiatus durations between mapped sedimentary packages and decompose estimated fossil-record incompleteness among nondeposition or erosion, preservation failure, and sampling. Dominance of long inter-formational hiatuses supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Hiatus duration and fossil incompleteness have correlated estimation errors.

The relative importance of causes varies by region and taxon.

fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.74

discriminating power: 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Gap durations are a native variable of open stratigraphic databases, and computing them against formation durations is a standard analysis a small team can do quickly. That settles whether separations are wide over a large part of the sedimentary record. It does not by itself show that those gaps, rather than the other biases Darwin listed, are the main source of imperfection, which is why the verdict stays partial.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure hiatus lengths between successive fossiliferous formations and compare them with the durations of the formations themselves. Gaps as long as or longer than the recorded intervals support wide unrecorded separations; continuously recorded succession would count against that pattern. Ranking gaps as the chief cause requires comparing their contribution with other biases.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Macrostrat coverage is much denser in some continents than worldwide.

Calling gaps the chief cause requires a model that partitions incompleteness among erosion, non-deposition, facies, and collection bias.

Unconformities can be brief locally and still look wide in a compiled column.

data existence: 0.86
